title: Persist channel drafts and inbound event deduplication
requirements: Implement a PostgreSQL ChannelPort adapter for ReadDraft, SaveDraft and ResetDraft over the accepted channel_identities, channel_events and conversation_drafts schema; a caller supplies or resolves an already trusted identity and the adapter never creates contacts or identities.

Use the accepted business_write_guard transaction order. Save and Reset atomically record a privacy-preserving event marker with the draft mutation; read returns no open draft after expiry, and mutation of an expired draft cannot revive its prior version.

Use positive optimistic versions: expected_version=0 creates only when no non-expired open draft exists; updates and resets require the current positive version. A stale event after change, reset, or expiry is rejected without mutation.

Deduplicate by platform plus integration plus a keyed digest of the trusted event identity. Same event plus the same normalized operation returns a stable safe result without mutation; a different normalized operation returns typed IDEMPOTENCY_MISMATCH. Persist no raw webhook payload, bot token, event ID, sender ID, conversation ID, or user answers in deduplication markers.
Do not implement SubmitInquiry, inquiry/notification-job creation, Telegram/VK SDKs, HTTP endpoints, outbound delivery, credentials, configuration, or migrations.
acceptance: Isolated disposable PostgreSQL tests prove create/read/update/reset, optimistic conflict atomicity, duplicate replay and mismatch, TELEGRAM/VK namespace separation, expiry handling, one-open-draft invariant, and rejected inputs/events causing no mutation.
The adapter uses only trusted ChannelContext and an explicit identity resolver/input boundary; user payload cannot alter context or manufacture an identity.
Every accepted draft mutation and event marker commits together under business_write_guard, while replays are stable and old events cannot advance a newer/reset/expired dialog.
The actual diff contains no migration, raw payload/token/PII persistence in markers, SDK, HTTP route, inquiry submission, notification or frontend work.

shared_paths_approval.reason: Accepted persistence adapter bound to existing bot contract and DB-004 schema, with no external transport or product submission side effects.
